items.title: 2.3 Product of two vectors (do vectors ko multiply karna) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 2.3 with Figs. 2.2 to 2.4 (PDF 25-28, printed 22-25).

blocks.text: Vectors ko do tarah multiply (zarb) kiya jata hai. In do types ke product (zarb ka jawab) ko scalar product aur vector product kehte hain.
Agar do vectors ko multiply karne se scalar quantity mile to use scalar product kehte hain, aur agar do vectors ko multiply karne se vector quantity mile to use vector product kehte hain.
Scalar or Dot Product (scalar ya dot product)
Do vectors A⃗ aur B⃗ ka scalar product A⃗.B⃗ likha jata hai (beech mein dot), aur is ki definition (tareef) yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.B⃗ = AB cos θ   (2.6)

blocks.text: Yahan A aur B vectors A⃗ aur B⃗ ki magnitudes hain aur θ un ke darmiyan angle hai.
Dot product ka physical matlab samajhne ke liye dono vectors ki tails (dumein) ek hi point (common origin) par rakhte hain (Fig. 2.2 a). Phir:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.B⃗ = A (projection of B⃗ on A⃗)

blocks.latex: \text{or}\quad \vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = A\,(\text{magnitude of component of } \vec{B} \text{ in the direction of } \vec{A}),\ \text{Fig. 2.2(b)}
blocks.text_alt: or A⃗.B⃗ = A (magnitude of component of B⃗ in the direction of A⃗), Fig. 2.2(b)

blocks.text: Yani B cos θ, vector B⃗ ka woh component hai jo A⃗ ki direction mein hai (Fig. 2.2 b):

blocks.text_alt: = A (B cos θ) = AB cos θ
Similarly, B⃗.A⃗ = B (A cos θ) = BA cos θ

blocks.alt: Do parts. (a) Vector A neeche seedha hai aur vector B usi origin se angle θ par uthta hai; B ke head se A tak dashed line girti hai, aur A ka woh hissa B cos θ likha hai. (b) A neeche seedha aur lamba B angle θ par; A ke head se dashed line B se 90° par milti hai, aur B ka woh hissa A cos θ likha hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.2: (a) B ka A par projection (saya) B cos θ; (b) A ka B par projection A cos θ (kitab ki Figure 2.2 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Yeh product hamein work (kaam) mein milta hai. Farz karein force F⃗ kisi cheez ko d distance tak le jati hai, aur motion ki direction F⃗ ki line of action ke saath angle θ banati hai (Fig. 2.3).

blocks.latex: \text{Work done} = (\text{Effective component of force in the direction of motion}) \times \text{Distance moved}
blocks.text_alt: Work done = (Effective component of force in the direction of motion) × Distance moved
= (F cos θ) d = Fd cos θ

blocks.text: Vector notation mein:

blocks.text_alt: F⃗.d⃗ = Fd cos θ = Work done

blocks.alt: Lakri ka block; us ke kone se force F horizontal (leti hui line) se angle theta par kheenchti hai. Displacement d horizontal direction mein hai; F ke head se us par dashed line girti hai, aur F cos theta F ka woh component hai jo d ke saath hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.3: Displacement d se angle θ par force F ka work (kitab ki Figure 2.3 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Characteristics of Scalar Product (scalar product ki khoobiyan)

1. A⃗.B⃗ = AB cos θ aur B⃗.A⃗ = BA cos θ = AB cos θ, is liye A⃗.B⃗ = B⃗.A⃗. Multiply karne ke order (tarteeb) se farq nahi parta; yani scalar product commutative (order badalne se jawab nahi badalta) hai.
2. Do perpendicular vectors (θ = 90°) ka scalar product zero hota hai, kyun ke cos 90° = 0.

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.B⃗ = AB cos 90° = 0

blocks.text: 3. Do parallel vectors ka scalar product un ki magnitudes ke product ke barabar hota hai. Parallel vectors (θ = 0°) ke liye cos 0° = 1:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.B⃗ = AB cos 0° = AB

blocks.text: Antiparallel (ulti direction wale) vectors (θ = 180°) ke liye cos 180° = -1:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.B⃗ = AB cos 180° = -AB

blocks.text: Kisi vector A⃗ ka apne aap se scalar product (self product) us ki magnitude ke square ke barabar hota hai:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.A⃗ = AA cos 0° = A²

blocks.text: Rectangular components ke zariye do vectors A⃗ aur B⃗ ka scalar product:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.B⃗ = AxBx + AyBy + AzBz   (2.7)

blocks.text: Equation (2.6) se do vectors ke darmiyan angle nikal sakte hain. Kyun ke

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.B⃗ = AB cos θ = AxBx + AyBy + AzBz
Therefore cos θ = (AxBx + AyBy + AzBz)/AB   (2.8)

blocks.text: Vector or Cross Product (vector ya cross product)
Do vectors A⃗ aur B⃗ ka vector product ek vector hai, jis ki definition yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗ × B⃗ = AB sin θ n̂   (2.9)

blocks.alt: Vectors A aur B ek rangeen plane (satah) mein hain, darmiyan angle theta. A x B dono ki common tail se seedha oopar, plane par perpendicular hai; saath chhota arrow unit vector n-hat hai, aur A x B ke gird ghoomta arrow A se B ki taraf rotation (ghumao) dikhata hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4(a): Vector product A × B, A aur B ke plane par perpendicular n̂ ke saath (kitab ki Figure 2.4(a) ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Yahan n̂ ek unit vector (magnitude 1 wala vector) hai jo A⃗ aur B⃗ wale plane (satah) par perpendicular hai (Fig. 2.4 a). Is ki direction right hand rule se maloom hoti hai: A⃗ aur B⃗ ki tails ek jagah rakhein; yeh dono ek plane banate hain. Product vector is plane par perpendicular hota hai. Pehle vector A⃗ ko chhote angle ke raste B⃗ ki taraf ghumayein, aur right hand (seedhe haath) ki ungliyan isi rotation ki taraf mor lein, angootha seedha khara rakhein. Seedha angootha product vector ki direction batata hai (Fig. 2.4 b). Isi rule ki wajah se B⃗ × A⃗, A⃗ × B⃗ ka ulta (opposite sign wala) vector hai (Fig. 2.4 c). Is liye:

blocks.alt: Wahi plane A, B aur theta ke saath. Oopar right hand, ungliyan A se B ki taraf mudi hui aur angootha seedha; angootha n-hat ki direction, yani A x B ki direction mein hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4(b): A × B ki direction ke liye right-hand rule (kitab ki Figure 2.4(b) ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.alt: Plane mein A, B aur theta, ab rotation B se A ki taraf. B x A common tail se seedha neeche hai, A x B ke ulat, gird ghoomte arrow ke saath.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4(c): B × A, A × B ke opposite (ulat) hai (kitab ki Figure 2.4(c) ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.alt: Ek point se angle theta par bane vectors A aur B ek rangeen parallelogram ki do adjacent (saath wali) sides hain; baqi do sides dashed hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4(d): A aur B ko adjacent sides bana kar bana parallelogram (kitab ki Figure 2.4(d) ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Characteristics of Cross Product (cross product ki khoobiyan)
1. A⃗ × B⃗ aur B⃗ × A⃗ barabar nahi, is liye cross product non-commutative (order badlo to jawab badal jata hai) hai:
2. Do perpendicular vectors (θ = 90°) ka cross product maximum (sab se zyada) magnitude ka hota hai, kyun ke sin 90° = 1:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗ × B⃗ = AB sin 90° n̂ = AB n̂

blocks.text: 3. Do parallel vectors ka cross product null vector (zero vector) hota hai, kyun ke un ke liye θ = 0° ya 180°, aur sin 0° = sin 180° = 0:

blocks.text_alt: A⃗ × B⃗ = AB sin 0° n̂ = 0 or A⃗ × B⃗ = AB sin 180° n̂ = 0

blocks.text: Isi wajah se A⃗ × A⃗ = 0 (θ = 0°).
4. A⃗ × B⃗ ki magnitude us parallelogram ke area ke barabar hai jis ki do adjacent sides (saath wali sides) A⃗ aur B⃗ hon (Fig. 2.4 d).
Examples of Vector Product (vector product ki misalein)

i. Jab kisi rigid body (aisi body jo shakal nahi badalti) par force F⃗ aise point par lagti hai jis ka position vector, ghoomne wali axis ke kisi point se, r⃗ hai, to force ka turning effect (ghumane wala asar), yani torque τ, r⃗ aur F⃗ ka vector product hai:
ii. Magnetic field B⃗ mein charge q aur velocity v⃗ wale particle (zarre) par force F⃗, v⃗ aur B⃗ ke vector product se milti hai:

blocks.caption: Dono products ka comparison (muqabla)
rows: A⃗ × B⃗ = AB sin θ n̂
A⃗ aur B⃗ ke plane par perpendicular vector (right hand rule)
torque τ⃗ = r⃗ × F⃗; F⃗ = q(v⃗ × B⃗)

blocks.prompt: Do vectors ke cross product aur scalar product ki magnitudes 4√3 aur 4 hain. Un ke darmiyan angle nikalein. Yeh bhi batayein ke dot product kab sab se zyada hota hai aur cross product kab.
blocks.explanation: AB sin θ = 4√3 aur AB cos θ = 4. Pehli ko doosri se divide karein: tan θ = √3, is liye θ = 60°. Dot product parallel vectors ke liye sab se zyada hai (cos θ = 1) aur cross product perpendicular vectors ke liye (sin θ = 1).

blocks.text: Summary (khulasa)

items: Dot product: A⃗.B⃗ = AB cos θ = A × (A⃗ par B⃗ ka projection) = AxBx + AyBy + AzBz; commutative; perpendicular ke liye 0, parallel ke liye AB, khud se A²; work = F⃗.d⃗.

Cross product: A⃗ × B⃗ = AB sin θ n̂, right hand rule se plane par perpendicular; A⃗ × B⃗ = -B⃗ × A⃗; perpendicular ke liye maximum, parallel ke liye null; magnitude = parallelogram ka area; torque r⃗ × F⃗, force q(v⃗ × B⃗).
